Candidate for owner approval (owner rule of 2026-10-06, carried from the shared development rules): consilience and expected observability. In sources, a practical effectiveness claim resting on one study or one evidence family is checked against independent streams, copies of one study count once, and real-world silence counts against a claimed effect only where the effect should be visible. For forum-signal checks, compare unique firsthand reports of the claimed effect with opposite and no-effect reports; separate objective outcomes from subjective impressions and actual experiences from questions, recommendations, speculation, reposts, and duplicate posters. Give approximate directional counts when feasible, classify the searched sample as common, mixed, minority, rare, absent, or indeterminate, state sampling limits, and never infer population incidence from forum frequency.
For a practical effectiveness claim a recommendation or ranking relies on (a device, software, therapy, supplement, or training method), especially a large or surprising effect from few studies, check that independent streams agree before treating it as established: independent replication, whether the thing sold is the thing tested, and real-world reports. Copies of one study count once. Real-world silence counts against a claimed effect only when the exact product is widely used and the effect would be noticeable to users who care about it; otherwise it is uninformative. Reviews and forums detect discrepancies; they are not trials. Classify the claim as convergent, promising but discordant, isolated, or contradicted.

  <Rule name="ConsilienceForPracticalEffectiveness" priority="Critical">
   For a practical effectiveness claim that a recommendation or ranking relies on, especially a large, surprising,
   fast, or commercially actionable effect resting on few studies, do not let one study or one evidence family carry
   the conclusion when materially independent streams are reasonably available. Fix the claim first: the exact
   intervention or preparation, population, comparator, outcome and its measurement, magnitude with units and
   uncertainty (EstimandFields/effect_magnitude), and duration. Then check the streams that can bear on it: independent
   replications and reviews; whether the material sold is the material studied; historical use, as a qualitative prior
   only (EvidenceLayerMisuseControl); firsthand reports where the effect should be noticeable
   (ExpectedObservabilityOfRealWorldTrace); and adjacent objective traces. Marketing copy, retailer listings, articles,
   and press releases that repeat one trial are one lineage (DuplicateAndDataLineageAudit). When the streams disagree,
   add to the discriminators above: trained versus untrained participants, learning effects on the test, and one sponsor
   or research group behind most of the studies. Classify the claim as convergent (independent streams agree on
   direction and rough magnitude), promising but discordant (formal evidence suggests benefit while other streams are
   weak or conflicting: state the mismatch and use a conservative magnitude, never the largest point estimate),
   isolated (one study, research group, sponsor-linked program, or evidence lineage: a lead, not an established
   effect), or contradicted (stronger independent evidence points the other way). An unexplained mismatch can justify
   calling an estimate likely inflated or non-generalizable without implying misconduct. No fixed number of streams is
   required, and a new, rare, or inaccessible intervention is not penalized for lacking reports.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="ExpectedObservabilityOfRealWorldTrace" priority="Critical">
   Before absent or no-effect firsthand reports count against a claimed benefit, check that the exact preparation is
   available, enough people use it, the outcome would be noticeable within ordinary use, and the searched communities or
   review corpora hold users who care about that outcome. When these mostly hold, a large claimed effect predicts a
   visible trace: search for positive, mixed, critical, and explicit no-effect reports with equal effort and in each
   language its users write in (DirectionalSearchSymmetry), and treat repeated absence or explicit no-effect reports as
   lowering confidence in the claimed magnitude or generality until explained, without proving that there is no effect.
   When they do not hold, as for an obscure, new, inaccessible, or rarely used product or an outcome users cannot
   perceive, classify the silence as weak or uninformative. Here reviews and forums are discrepancy detectors and
   evidence of heterogeneity, not informal trials: never estimate an effect size or incidence from them
   (SilentDenominator, ConsilienceForPracticalEffectiveness).
  </Rule>

  <Case id="LargeTrialEffectSilentRealWorld">
   <Prompt>
    One small trial reports 15 to 20 kg more strength after several weeks of an extract widely sold to gym users.
    Large retailer review sets and lifting forums mostly mention other effects, and experienced lifters report no
    strength change. Rank it among strength supplements.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Do not rank it by the trial's point estimate. Check training status, measurement, sponsor dependence, and
    replication; classify the strength effect as isolated or promising but discordant until the mismatch is explained,
    and rank it by a conservative magnitude.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="TraditionalStrengthLabelModernEndpoint">
   <Prompt>
    A traditional text calls a plant strengthening, and sellers cite it as confirmation of large barbell-strength
    gains.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Keep the traditional use as documented use and a discovery prior; do not treat it as evidence of a
    one-repetition-maximum gain without evidence that the meanings match.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="UnderexposedProductNoReports">
   <Prompt>
    A specialized extract has few buyers and no active user community, and no firsthand reports can be found.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Mark the real-world stream as underexposed and the silence as uninformative: it neither supports nor weakens the
    claimed effect.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="ManyPagesOneTrial">
   <Prompt>
    Retailers, blogs, and press releases all cite the same trial as proof that a supplement works.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Count them as one evidence lineage, not as independent confirmation.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
